title: Battle of Antonov Airport at Hostomel near Kyiv
body:
The Battle of Antonov Airport, also called the Battle of Hostomel Airport, was fought on 24 and 25 February 2022 at Antonov Airport in Hostomel, Kyiv Oblast, about 10 kilometres from Kyiv. It formed part of the northern front of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Russian planners sought to seize the airfield and use it as an airbridge to bring in forces against the capital.

On 24 February, Russian Airborne Forces launched a helicopter-borne assault. Reported Russian units included the 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade and the 45th Guards Spetsnaz Brigade. The airport was defended by roughly 200 to 300 troops of Ukraine's National Guard 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade, later reinforced by army units including the 72nd Mechanized Brigade. Ukrainian fire and portable air-defence missiles downed at least two helicopters. Russian paratroopers captured the airport that day, but Ukrainian counterattacks encircled them and pushed them back by evening.

On 25 February Russia launched a second air assault, supported by armoured forces that advanced from Belarus, and retook the airport. Estimates of the forces involved and of casualties vary widely. Ukrainian reporting claimed 300 to 500 Russian paratroopers killed, while Russia claimed about 200 Ukrainian dead. The An-225 Mriya, the world's largest aeroplane, was destroyed in its hangar. The runways were heavily damaged, and analysts generally judge that the Ukrainian defence delayed the Russian airbridge. Ukraine regained the airport on 2 April 2022.
